medium.title: Cycling in the City
paras: Over the past two decades, many cities have tried to reduce traffic congestion by encouraging residents to cycle. {{This policy}} has proved popular, although it requires a significant investment in infrastructure.
Copenhagen is often cited as a model. Its network of protected lanes allows cyclists to travel safely across the city, and as a result around half of all commuters now choose {{it}} over driving.

Critics, however, argue that the approach cannot be copied everywhere. Cities with steep hills or extreme weather face obstacles that {{their}} flatter, milder counterparts do not, and this limits the benefits.

Nevertheless, experts suggest that electric bikes may overcome these barriers. {{They}} reduce the effort needed to climb hills, which makes cycling realistic for older people. If {{this trend}} continues, cycling could become a mainstream form of transport.
